However, if a person of ordinary skill in the art, after reading the patent claims, specification, and patent prosecution history, can clearly and reasonably understand that the protected object must be used in such a use environment, then the use environment feature should be understood to require that the protected object must be used in that specific environment. Claim 1 of the patent in this case defines two use environment features for the protected rear derailleur bracket, which are analyzed separately as follows:

First, regarding use environment feature 1 (i.e., the structural feature of the bicycle frame). The patent application in this case underwent multiple amendments during the substantive examination process. In response to the first Office Action from the National Intellectual Property Administration, which cited Document 1 (US Patent No. US5082303), in order to distinguish the rear derailleur bracket sought to be protected in this patent application from the suspension member (18) disclosed in that document, Shimano Inc. explicitly stated in a Statement of Opinion that the suspension member (18) described in Document 1 is part of a vertical drop assembly, and that the combination of the vertical drop member (16), the suspension member (18), and the device (16) for connecting the suspension member to the drop member is equivalent to the structure of the rear fork end (51) with the rear derailleur mounting extension (14) in the patent application of this case. According to Shimano Inc., the rear derailleur bracket protected by the patent in this case can only be connected to a rear fork end with a rear derailleur mounting extension and cannot become a constituent part of the vertical drop assembly of the rear fork end of the bicycle frame. In response to the second Office Action, which cited Document 2 (European Patent EP0013136), in order to distinguish the rear derailleur bracket sought to be protected in this patent application from the drop assembly disclosed in that document, Shimano Inc. explicitly stated that the fork end described in that document is a horizontally slotted drop assembly, and that document does not disclose or suggest the features of the present invention application, particularly that the bracket body is not connected to the vertical drop assembly or an L-shaped plate. This statement indicates that the rear derailleur bracket protected by this patent must be installed on a rear fork end of a bicycle frame having a derailleur mounting extension, and cannot be installed on a rear fork end of a bicycle frame having a horizontally slotted drop assembly. Therefore, for use environment feature 1, it should be understood that the bicycle rear derailleur bracket protected by the patent in this case must be used on a rear fork end of a bicycle frame having use environment feature 1.

Second, regarding use environment feature 2 (i.e., the structural feature of the rear derailleur). In response to the second Office Action from the National Intellectual Property Administration, which cited Document 3 (US Patent No. US4690663), in order to distinguish the rear derailleur bracket sought to be protected in this patent application from the base member 1 disclosed in that document, Shimano Inc. again amended Claim 1, adding structural features regarding the rear derailleur. Shimano Inc. explicitly stated in a Statement of Opinion that the base member 1 mentioned in that document is actually a component of the four-bar linkage mechanism of the derailleur, one end of which is connected to the threaded hole 101b on the derailleur mounting extension of the rear fork end of the bicycle frame through a horizontal shaft 6 and a through hole 11; therefore, the base member 1 is not equivalent to the bracket body 8 in the present application. Shimano Inc. further pointed out that the derailleur disclosed in Document 3 is directly installed on the derailleur mounting extension of the rear fork end of the bicycle frame. In contrast, the present invention discloses a bicycle rear derailleur bracket for connecting a rear derailleur (100) to a bicycle frame (50), wherein the rear derailleur has a bracket member (5), a support member (4) for supporting a chain guide device (3), and a pair of connecting members (6, 7) for connecting the support member (4) and the bracket member (5). The present invention connects the bracket member (5) of the rear derailleur to one end of the bracket body (8) of the bracket, and then connects the other end of the bracket body (8) to the derailleur mounting extension (14) of the rear fork end (51) of the bicycle frame. According to Shimano Inc., the rear derailleur bracket protected by this patent must be connected to the bracket member (5) of the rear derailleur and cannot become a component of the rear derailleur itself. It can be seen that the rear derailleur bracket protected by this patent must be used on a rear derailleur having the bracket member (5), the support member (4) for supporting the chain guide device (3), and the pair of connecting members (6, 7) for connecting the support member (4) and the bracket member (5) as described in Claim 1. Therefore, for use environment feature 2, it should be understood that the bicycle rear derailleur bracket protected by the patent in this case must be used on a rear derailleur having use environment feature 2.

In summary, the use environment features of the patent in this case have a limiting effect on the scope of protection, and the bicycle rear derailleur bracket protected by the patent in this case must be used in that use environment. Shimano Inc.'s ground for retrial, that the use environment features appearing in the claims of the patent in this case do not constitute necessary technical features of the patent in this case and do not affect the scope of protection of the claims, cannot be established and is not supported.

(B) Whether the accused infringing product in this case is necessarily used on the bicycle frame defined by Claim 1 of the patent in this case

The accused infringing product in this case has the structural features of the bracket body as defined in Claim 1 and the use environment features of the rear derailleur, which is not disputed by the parties. Additionally, evidence provided by Shimano Inc., such as the Notarial Certificate (2005) Hu Huang Yi Zheng Jing Zi No. 5137 and the Notarial Certificate (2005) Hang Gong Zheng Jing Zi No. 475, can prove that the accused infringing product has also been actually applied to bicycle frames having the features defined in Claim 1 of the patent in this case. This is also not disputed by the parties. The issue disputed by the parties is whether the accused infringing product in this case is necessarily used on the bicycle frame defined by Claim 1 of the patent in this case, or whether the accused infringing product can be applied to a bicycle frame that does not have the features described in Claim 1 of the patent in this case. An analysis of this is as follows:

First, the specific structure of the accused infringing product in this case determines its specific matching relationship with the bicycle frame described in the claim. Based on the facts found by this court, the accused infringing product has a protruding portion extending upward from the surface of the plate near the position of the bolt hole away from the rear derailleur. This protruding portion objectively needs to cooperate with a specific position of the rear fork end of the bicycle frame in order to achieve a positioning function.

Second, the actual demonstration by the parties during the original trial can assist in illustrating the actual installation state of the accused infringing product. To prove that the accused infringing product can be installed on a bicycle frame without a rear fork end extension, Richen Company installed the accused infringing product directly on a bicycle frame without a rear fork end extension by adding a washer between the accused infringing product and the rear fork end of the frame to compensate for the gap caused by the protruding portion of the accused infringing product. However, Richen Company did not include a washer when selling the accused infringing product externally. This installation method is not a typical industrial production method and would affect the positioning effect. Furthermore, regarding this court's request for evidence of a bicycle that has the accused infringing product installed on a bicycle frame without a rear fork end extension and that has been commercially circulated in the market, Richen Company has consistently failed to provide such evidence.

Finally, the relevant industry standards for bicycle frames can assist in proving the actual installation state of the accused infringing product. The "Industry Standard of the People's Republic of China - Bicycle Industry Standard - Bicycle Frames" (QB1880-93) is a mandatory industry standard issued by the former Ministry of Light Industry of China, which discloses two types of horizontal dropout plates for bicycle frames, one having a rear fork end extension and the other not having a rear fork end extension. The bicycle frame having the rear fork end extension possesses the limiting features of the frame in Claim 1 of the patent. Since installing the accused infringing product on a bicycle frame without a rear fork end extension is not a typical industrial production method and affects the positioning effect, installing the accused infringing product on a bicycle frame having a rear fork end extension becomes almost an inevitable choice.

It can be seen that installing the accused infringing product on a bicycle frame having a rear fork end extension is the only reasonable commercial use for the accused infringing product. In the absence of further effective counter-evidence submitted by Richen Company, it can be considered that the accused infringing product in this case is commercially necessarily used on the bicycle frame defined by Claim 1 of the patent in this case.

(C) Whether the accused infringing product in this case falls within the scope of protection of the patent in this case

First, the scope of protection of Claim 1 of the patent in this case needs to be clarified. According to the description of Claim 1 of the patent in this case, its scope of protection is defined by the following essential technical features: 1. Use environment feature: A bicycle rear derailleur bracket for connecting a rear derailleur to a bicycle frame, wherein the rear derailleur has a bracket member, a support member for supporting a chain guide device, and a pair of connecting members for connecting the support member and the bracket member, and the bicycle frame has a connecting structure formed on a derailleur mounting extension of a rear fork end of the bicycle frame. 2. Rear derailleur bracket structural feature: a bracket body formed of a substantially L-shaped plate; a first connecting structure provided near one end of the bracket body, for connecting the bracket member of the rear derailleur to the bracket body, rotatable about a first axis; a second connecting structure provided near the other end of the bracket body, for connecting the bracket body to the connecting structure of the bicycle frame; and a positioning structure for contacting the derailleur mounting extension so as to position the rear derailleur relative to the rear fork end in a predetermined posture. 3. Positional feature after installation of the rear derailleur bracket: the arrangement of the first connecting structure and the second connecting structure shall be such that when the bracket body is mounted on the rear fork end, the connection point provided by the first connecting structure is below and behind the connection point provided by the second connecting structure.

Second, regarding the comparison of technical features. Based on the foregoing, the accused infringing product in this case is commercially necessarily used on the bicycle frame defined by Claim 1 of the patent in this case, and therefore the accused infringing product possesses the use environment feature regarding the bicycle frame in Claim 1. Meanwhile, the accused infringing product possesses the structural features of the bracket body and the use environment features of the rear derailleur as described in Claim 1. Therefore, the accused infringing product possesses all the features of Claim 1 except for the positional feature after installation of the rear derailleur bracket.

Finally, regarding the positional feature after installation of the rear derailleur bracket. The accused infringing product has a protruding portion extending upward from the surface of the plate near the position of the bolt hole away from the rear derailleur. Since the accused infringing product in this case is commercially necessarily used on the bicycle frame defined by Claim 1 of the patent in this case, when the protruding portion of the accused infringing product is matched and installed with the bicycle frame described in the claim, the positional relationship characteristic that the connection point provided by the first connecting structure is below and behind the connection point provided by the second connecting structure will inevitably be presented.

Therefore, the accused infringing product possesses all the technical features of Claim 1 of the patent in this case and falls within the scope of protection of Claim 1 of the patent in this case. Shimano Inc.'s corresponding ground for retrial is established and should be supported.

(D) Whether the respondent's prior art defense is established

The prior art asserted by Richen Company includes two types: first, the suspension member disclosed in Document 1 (US Patent No. US4690663) submitted in the invalidation proceeding combined with common general knowledge; second, the combination of Figure 2, Figure 6, and Figure 10 of the "Light Industry Industry Standard of the People's Republic of China - Bicycle Derailleurs" (QB/T 1895-1993) and Figure 10 of the "Industry Standard of the People's Republic of China - Bicycle Industry Standard - Bicycle Frames" (QB1880-93).

Regarding the first prior art defense. Since the suspension member described in US Patent No. US4690663 is part of a vertical drop assembly, and the combination of the vertical drop member, the suspension member, and the device for connecting the suspension member to the drop member is equivalent to the structure of the rear fork end with the rear derailleur mounting extension in the patent application of this case, therefore there is no correspondence between this suspension member and the rear derailleur bracket protected by the patent in this case. Furthermore, even if it were determined that the suspension member corresponds to the rear derailleur bracket protected by the patent in this case, that patent also does not disclose technical features such as the bracket body being L-shaped, and the evidence submitted by Richen Company cannot prove that designing the bracket body in an L-shape was common general knowledge among persons of ordinary skill in the art before the filing date of the patent application in this case. Therefore, this prior art defense cannot be established.

Regarding the second prior art defense. Figure 2, Figure 6, and Figure 10 of the "Light Industry Industry Standard of the People's Republic of China - Bicycle Derailleurs" (QB/T 1895-1993) disclose a derailleur tab installed on a bicycle frame without a rear fork end extension. This tab has a different use environment from that defined by the patent in this case and does not disclose the features of the rear derailleur bracket being L-shaped and the positioning structure on the bracket as described in the patent in this case. Figure 10 of the "Industry Standard of the People's Republic of China - Bicycle Industry Standard - Bicycle Frames" (QB1880-93) discloses a bicycle frame having a rear fork end extension. Therefore, even if the two are combined, they still do not disclose the features of the rear derailleur bracket being L-shaped and the positioning structure on the bracket as described in the patent in this case. This prior art defense is also not established.

(E) Whether the proceedings in this case should be stayed

Richen Company requested during the retrial proceedings of this court to stay the trial of this case. The patent in this case is an invention patent. According to Article 11 of the Supreme People's Court's Several Provisions on Issues Concerning the Application of Law in Trial of Patent Dispute Cases, the people's court may decide not to stay the proceedings. Furthermore, after trial, this court has already ascertained the facts and legal issues of this case and can reach a conclusion. It is not necessary to rely on the outcome of the invalidation proceeding as the basis for this case. The people's court may decide not to stay the proceedings. Therefore, the above claim of Richen Company is not supported by this court.

(F) Regarding the assumption of civil liability in this case

Since the accused infringing product in this case falls within the scope of protection of the patent in this case, the acts of Richen Company in manufacturing and selling the accused infringing product constitute infringement of the patent right in this case, and Richen Company shall assume civil liability for ceasing the infringement, eliminating danger, and compensating for losses.

Regarding the specific forms of civil liability, this Court analyzes and evaluates as follows in light of Shimano Inc.'s claims:

First, the evidence in this case shows that Richen Company manufactured and sold the infringing products, and such manufacturing and sales activities are ongoing. An order to cease manufacturing and selling the infringing products is one of the necessary measures to stop the infringement. This Court supports Shimano Inc.'s claim for an order that Richen Company immediately cease manufacturing and selling the infringing products.

Second, destruction of any remaining unsold infringing products is one of the necessary measures to eliminate danger and prevent the infringing products from entering the sales channels. If Richen Company possesses any unsold infringing products, they shall be destroyed. This Court supports Shimano Inc.'s claim for an order that Richen Company destroy all remaining infringing products.

Third, the court of first instance, upon Shimano Inc.'s application, conducted evidence preservation at Richen Company's place of business. However, upon inspection, no dedicated molds for manufacturing the infringing products, the RD-HG-30A and RD-HG-40A bicycle rear derailleurs, were found. The existing evidence in this case cannot prove that dedicated molds are required to manufacture the infringing products. This Court does not support Shimano Inc.'s claim for an order that Richen Company destroy dedicated molds for manufacturing the infringing products.

Fourth, Richen Company printed images of the infringing products, the RD-HG-30A and RD-HG-40A bicycle rear derailleurs, in its product brochures from different periods. Such conduct constitutes an offer for sale. Destruction of undistributed promotional materials bearing images of the infringing products is one of the necessary measures to eliminate danger. If Richen Company possesses undistributed promotional materials bearing images of the infringing products, they shall be destroyed. This Court supports Shimano Inc.'s claim for an order that Richen Company destroy remaining promotional materials bearing images of the infringing products.

Fifth, Shimano Inc. did not submit evidence in this case to prove that Richen Company published advertisements for the infringing products on the Internet. Richen Company also does not admit to publishing such advertisements. Therefore, this Court does not support Shimano Inc.'s claim for an order that Richen Company delete advertisements relating to the infringing products from the Internet.

Sixth, Shimano Inc. did not provide sufficient evidence in this case to prove the losses it suffered due to the infringement or the profits gained by the infringer from the infringement, nor is there a patent license fee that can be used as a reference. This Court shall reasonably determine the amount of damages with reference to factors such as the type of patent right, the nature and circumstances of the infringement, etc. During the first instance proceedings, Shimano Inc. incurred expenses for this case including RMB 80 for purchasing the infringing product, RMB 1,000 for evidence preservation, RMB 592.5 for consulting industrial and commercial administrative records, RMB 750 for translation fees, and RMB 1,170.35 for travel expenses, totaling RMB 3,592.85. These expenses were all necessary for investigating and stopping the infringement in this case. During the first instance proceedings, Shimano Inc. also submitted a statistical statement of legal service fees, invoices for attorney fees, and a credit notice from CITIC Industrial Bank as evidence to prove the attorney fees already paid for this case. According to the statistical statement of legal service fees submitted by Shimano Inc., calculated at RMB 3,000 per attorney per hour, the total attorney fees as of July 2004 amounted to RMB 442,500. The amount of this fee is consistent with and mutually corroborated by the invoices for attorney fees and the credit notice from CITIC Industrial Bank. Although Richen Company challenged the amount of the said attorney fees, it did not provide sufficient facts or reasons, and charging attorney fees at RMB 3,000 per hour does not violate the provisions of relevant laws, administrative regulations, or administrative rules. This Court supports this claim. During the second instance proceedings of this case, to prove that the infringing product could only be installed on the rear fork end of a bicycle frame having a connector structure with a derailleur-mounting extension as defined in the patent-in-suit, Shimano Inc. conducted additional evidence preservation by notarization. During the retrial proceedings of this case, to prove that Richen Company's alleged infringing acts were ongoing, Shimano Inc. again conducted evidence preservation by notarization. Although Shimano Inc. did not provide relevant receipts to prove the evidence preservation expenses incurred after the conclusion of the first instance, the notarization mandate had actually occurred, and notary fees were objectively required. This Court takes this into consideration when determining the amount of damages. During the court hearing of this Court, Shimano Inc. asserted that its claimed economic loss of RMB 300,000 included the reasonable expenses it had incurred. Given that the reasonable expenses Shimano Inc. incurred for investigating and stopping the infringement in this case already exceed its claimed amount of RMB 300,000, this Court fully supports its claim for an order that Richen Company pay RMB 300,000 in damages.

In conclusion, the alleged infringing product in this case falls within the scope of protection of the patent-in-suit. Richen Company's acts of manufacturing and selling the RD-HG-30A and RD-HG-40A bicycle rear derailleur products infringe Shimano Inc.'s patent right in this case. The court of original trial made some errors in fact-finding and improperly applied the law, which should be corrected. Pursuant to Article 56, Paragraph 1 of the Patent Law of the People's Republic of China (as amended in 2000), and Articles 186, Paragraph 1, and 153, Paragraph 1, Items (2) and (3) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the judgment is as follows:

1. Set aside the Civil Judgment (2009) Zhe Min Zai Zi No. 135 of the Zhejiang High People's Court, the Civil Judgment (2005) Zhe Min San Zhong Zi No. 145, and the Civil Judgment (2004) Yong Min Er Chu Zi No. 240 of the Ningbo Intermediate People's Court;

2. Ningbo Richen Industry & Trade Co., Ltd. shall immediately cease manufacturing and selling the RD-HG-30A and RD-HG-40A bicycle rear derailleurs that fall within the scope of protection of Invention Patent No. ZL94102612.4, and shall destroy any remaining infringing products and promotional materials bearing images of the infringing products;

3. Within fifteen days from the date of service of this judgment, Ningbo Richen Industry & Trade Co., Ltd. shall compensate Shimano Inc. for the losses caused by the infringement in this case and the reasonable expenses incurred for investigating and stopping the infringement, totaling RMB 300,000;

4. Dismiss Shimano Inc.'s other claims.

If the obligation to pay money is not fulfilled within the period specified in this judgment, interest on the debt for delayed performance shall be doubled in accordance with Article 229 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China.

The first instance case acceptance fee is RMB 7,010, and the evidence preservation fee is RMB 1,000, totaling RMB 8,010. The second instance case acceptance fee is RMB 7,010. All fees shall be borne by Ningbo Richen Industry & Trade Co., Ltd.

This judgment is final.
